FN-8ZP3H2-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 492
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Representative Jim Hill
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 05/23/2023
House Bill 492 as introduced could increase the administrative obligations of the
Administrative Office of Courts to: (1) develop and maintain the list of all requests from judges
to keep certain personal information from being published on governmental agencies websites;
and (2) notify the appropriate officers of all governmental entities quarterly of any requests
received.
In addition, this bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund from fines; increase
receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds and other funds to which court costs are
deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, the
Bureau of Pardons and Paroles, the Department of Corrections, and community corrections
programs by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and
convicted of the offenses provided by the bill and the penalties imposed.

FN-8ZP3H2-3
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 492
Committee: Judiciary Sponsor: Representative Jim Hill
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 05/30/2023
House Bill 492 as passed the House of Representatives could increase the administrative
obligations of the Administrative Office of Courts to: (1) develop and maintain the list of all
requests from judges to keep certain personal information from being published on
governmental agencies websites; and (2) notify the appropriate officers of all governmental
entities quarterly of any requests received.
This bill could also increase the administrative obligations of certain government agencies to
remove certain personal information regarding judicial officers from the agencies' websites and
redact this information on public records requests.
In addition, this bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund from fines; increase
receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds and other funds to which court costs are
deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district attorneys, the
Bureau of Pardons and Paroles, the Department of Corrections, and community corrections
programs by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons charged with and
convicted of the offenses provided by the bill and the penalties imposed.
